title: Evidence collector playbook for data residency & retention controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and automated pipeline to collect, normalize, and store evidence for data residency and retention controls required by SOC 2 and ISO 27001. The playbook will define control mappings, collectors (logs, configs, snapshots), artifact formats, retention for evidence itself, and reporting hooks for the Compliance team and external auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Control mapping doc that ties each SOC 2 and ISO 27001 clause to one or more evidence artifacts and collectors
Automated collectors implemented for at least three distinct evidence types (config snapshot, retention policy export, residency-tagged manifest) with repeatable runbook
Evidence artifacts stored in an immutable archive bucket with tamper-evident naming and checksum, retention for evidence defined
Console/Report view that can export a per-control evidence package (zip with artifacts and mapping) for auditor requests
End-to-end test demonstrating collection, archive, and retrieval for a sample customer project in eu-west-1 region
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Security and Compliance; reviewed SOC 2 requirements and ISO 27001 annex A controls relevant to data residency and retention.
2026-03-04: Draft control-to-artifact mapping completed (v0.1) and shared with Legal and Security for feedback.
2026-03-08: Engineering spike approved; ENG-4128 to build an 'evidence-export' microservice to run collectors on schedule.
2026-03-10: Design review with Console team to surface 'Export Evidence' action; prototype wireframes attached in Confluence.
2026-03-12: Security requested KMS proof-of-ownership artifact and stronger immutability guarantees for archived evidence; added as dependency ENG-4210.
decisions: Use immutable S3 object lock with versioning in dedicated 'evidence-archive' buckets per region for archived artifacts.
Store a control mapping YAML in the archive alongside artifacts to make packages self-describing.
Evidence collectors will be idempotent and sign artifacts with a platform HSM-backed signing key; signature metadata stored in manifest.json.
control_mappings: SOC2: CC6.3 / CC7.1 -> Evidence: data residency manifest (per-tenant region tag), proof of routing policy enforcement, archive of routing logs
SOC2: CC9.3 -> Evidence: retention policy export (S3 lifecycle rules, DB retention schedules), sample deletion audit for a retired dataset
ISO27001: A.8.3 (Handling of assets) -> Evidence: inventory export + residency attribute, retention classification labels
ISO27001: A.12.4 (Logging) -> Evidence: signed log snapshots and retention lifecycle metadata
Cross-cutting -> Evidence: role-provisioning snapshot, KMS key rotation history, and signed manifest tying artifacts to a control id
collectors_plan: config_snapshot_collector: daily snapshot of IAM policies, S3 bucket configs, VPC region tags; output JSON compressed and signed
retention_policy_exporter: weekly export of DB table retention settings and S3 lifecycle rules, plus example delete job logs
residency_manifest_generator: on-deploy hook that emits a per-tenant residency manifest for assets created in a region; stored with object lifecycle metadata
logging_snapshot_agent: scheduled aggregation of application and infra logs for the retention window requested by auditors (with sampling controls)
evidence_archiver: moves collector outputs to region-specific evidence-archive bucket, applies object-lock and writes manifest.json with checksums and signature
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Evidence collection could include sensitive customer data. Mitigation: collectors must redact PII, and archiver will enforce access control and limited retention of raw logs.
Risk: Archival costs grow unbounded. Mitigation: tiered retention policies for evidence artifacts and policy to expire low-value artifacts after X years; include cost estimate in runbook.
Risk: Auditor requests for on-prem/private deployments. Mitigation: build a signed export format and lightweight collector that customers can run in their VPC and upload to our secure intake API.
